9:Evaluating an LLM on a full benchmark is costly, so we run it on n ≪ N items and predict its full score. Existing methods (anchor points, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, assessor, active acquisition) use the score matrix of *source models* to pick items and fit a *latent model* of the target; they are judged mostly on held-out models that resemble the sources. We cast the problem as **finite-population estimation of a mean of N unknown 0/1 values with a free covariate (the source matrix)**. That frame separates what the sources can buy — **variance reduction** — from what must be controlled by design — **bias**. We (i) test, on 13 binary matrices and under three target splits (interpolation, extrapolation, lineage-held-out), whether model-based predictors lose accuracy where targets differ from the sources; (ii) test whether a design-based correction (probability sampling with a positivity floor + difference/GREG estimator) repairs it and at what variance cost; (iii) measure how much the source matrix can help at all over plain stratified/balanced random sampling; (iv) examine ordering of models separately from score error.
